what: Block-average predictions: mean and standard deviation
title: From point-sampled plots to a paddock block mean
text: change--support problem set general Cressie (1993) surveyed Gotway Young (2002): point process (plots) aggregated areal one (blocks). gpfield approximates block average tensor-midpoint quadrature nqn_q nodes inside block footprint, equal weights wj=1/nqw_j = 1 / n_q. Writing K*nK_{*n} covariance nqn_q quadrature nodes nn training points, KnK_n training covariance, K**K_{**} quadrature nodes’ covariance, block mean variance ŷB=∑j=1nqwj[K*nKn−1y]j,Var(yB)=w⊤(K**−K*nKn−1Kn*)w. \hat{y}_B = \sum_{j=1}^{n_q} w_j \, \big[K_{*n} K_n^{-1} y\big]_j, \qquad \mathrm{Var}(y_B) = w^\top \big(K_{**} - K_{*n} K_n^{-1} K_{n*}\big) w. posterior mean covariance point prediction use, evaluated quadrature nodes averaged quadrature weights, block variance carries full within-block posterior covariance rather marginal point-wise variances alone. Block-average predictions south north halves county C1.
code: block_pred <- gp_predict(fit, support = "block", blocks = blocks, seed = 1L) block_tab <- data.frame(   block = block_pred@locations$block,   mean = round(block_pred@mean, 1L),   sd = round(block_pred@sd, 2L),   n_support = block_pred@n_support )

what: Why this is not a cell-wise average
title: From point-sampled plots to a paddock block mean
text: naive mean nqn_q point predictions treat independent shrink block-average standard deviation 1/nq1 / \sqrt{n_q}. neighbouring plots within block positively correlated, change--support variance materially larger. Change--support standard deviation naive independence assumption, 196 quadrature nodes.
code: centre <- gp_predict(fit, data.frame(row = 5, col = 6)) # The tensor-midpoint rule realises per_axis^2 nodes, per_axis = # round(sqrt(n_quad)), not the requested n_quad exactly -- divide by the # realised count, not the request. per_axis <- max(2L, round(sqrt(blocks$n_quad))) n_realised <- per_axis^2L naive_sd <- centre@sd / sqrt(n_realised) sd_compare <- data.frame(   quantity = c("change-of-support SD (south block)",                "naive independence SD (centre point / sqrt(n))"),   sd = round(c(block_pred@sd[[1L]], naive_sd), 3L) )

what: Abstention: when the data will not bear the answer
title: From point-sampled plots to a paddock block mean
text: gpfield refuses prediction data support, returning typed gpfield_abstention machine-readable reason rather confident surface built data sparse coarse carry . Two refusals , triggered real fit , read numbers Read section.
code: # A query grid spaced far more coarsely than the estimated range. coarse <- gp_predict(fit, data.frame(row = c(1, 50, 100),                                      col = c(1, 50, 100))) is_gpfield_abstention(coarse) #> [1] TRUE coarse #> <gpfield_abstention> #>   scope:  gp_predict #>   reason: range_too_short #>   detail: query spacing 69.3 exceeds 1 x the estimated range 13.67; the field cannot be resolved this finely #>     spacing = 69.3 #>     range = 13.67 #>     spacing_tol = 1 # A block placed far outside the trial footprint. far <- block_support(lower = rbind(c(100, 100)), upper = rbind(c(110, 110))) far_pred <- gp_predict(fit, support = "block", blocks = far, seed = 1L) is_gpfield_abstention(far_pred) #> [1] TRUE far_pred #> <gpfield_abstention> #>   scope:  gp_predict #>   reason: support_gap #>   detail: block block1 has no training observation within 13.67 (1 range) of its footprint #>     block = block1 #>     range = 13.67 #>     reach = 13.67

title: From point-sampled plots to a paddock block mean
text: exact solver cubic number observations – comfortable hundreds--low-thousands plots multi-environment trial carries, much larger field. solver = "lowrank" fits Deterministic Training Conditional (DTC) sparse Gaussian process (Quinonero-Candela Rasmussen 2005) set mm space-filling inducing points, cost linear number plots nn quadratic inducing count. Writing KnmK_{nm} covariance training points inducing points KmmK_{mm} inducing points’ covariance, DTC replaces exact n×nn \times n training covariance KnK_n rank-mm approximation Kn≈KnmKmm−1Kmn, K_n \approx K_{nm} K_{mm}^{-1} K_{mn}, every quantity otherwise need n×nn \times n Cholesky factorisation instead needs m×mm \times m one. Every verb – point block prediction, change support, abstention, manifest emission – unchanged; backend differs. section needs real trial data, runs regardless agridat: synthetic field, labelled , two smooth sinusoidal gradients plus noise. inducing set covers whole field low-rank posterior exactly exact GP, choice scale-versus-cost dial rather change model; default backend stays exact.
code: set.seed(1L) big <- expand.grid(x = seq(0, 25, by = 0.5), y = seq(0, 25, by = 0.5)) big$yield <- sin(0.3 * big$x) + cos(0.25 * big$y) + rnorm(nrow(big), 0, 0.2) nrow(big) #> [1] 2601  fit_lr <- gp_fit(   gpfield_spec(c("x", "y"), "yield", solver = "lowrank", n_inducing = 120L),   big, seed = 1L ) fit_lr #> <gpfield_fit> #>   kernel:      matern #>   n training:  2601 #>   solver:      low-rank (DTC, 120 inducing points) #>   length-scale (standardised): 4.496 #>   range (raw units):           90.66 #>   marginal var / noise var:    10.35 / 0.04111 #>   log marginal likelihood:     326.7

code: library(gpfield)  # A noisy field on a 10 x 10 plot grid. set.seed(1L) field <- expand.grid(row = seq_len(10L), col = seq_len(10L)) field$yield <- 3 + 0.3 * field$row + sin(field$col / 2) +   rnorm(nrow(field), 0, 0.2)  # Fit the GP. fit <- gp_fit(gpfield_spec(c("row", "col"), "yield"), field, seed = 1L) fit #> <gpfield_fit> #>   kernel:      matern #>   n training:  100 #>   length-scale (standardised): 4.34 #>   range (raw units):           34.31 #>   marginal var / noise var:    3.317 / 0.02171 #>   log marginal likelihood:     10.6  # Predict two paddock-scale block averages (change of support). blocks <- block_support(   lower = rbind(c(1, 1), c(6, 6)),   upper = rbind(c(5, 5), c(10, 10)) ) gp_predict(fit, support = "block", blocks = blocks, seed = 1L) #> <gpfield_prediction> #>   support:   block #>   locations: 2 #>   mean range: [4.725, 4.778] #>   sd range:   [0.03812, 0.03812]  # Ask for a resolution the field cannot support: gpfield abstains. gp_predict(fit, data.frame(row = c(1, 60), col = c(1, 60))) #> <gpfield_abstention> #>   scope:  gp_predict #>   reason: range_too_short #>   detail: query spacing 83.44 exceeds 1 x the estimated range 34.31; the field cannot be resolved this finely #>     spacing = 83.44 #>     range = 34.31 #>     spacing_tol = 1

title: Specify a gpfield Gaussian-process model — gpfield_spec
text: coords Character vector naming spatial coordinate columns (one transect, two field, three caller projected additional spatial axes). time column also given, appended coordinate set extra, separately-scaled axis. response Character scalar naming response column smooth. kernel Character covariance kernel: "matern" (default) "se" (squared-exponential). nu Matern smoothness; one 0.5, 1.5 (default) 2.5. Ignored squared-exponential kernel. time Optional character scalar naming time column spatio-temporal fit, NA (default) purely spatial model. time axis present fit anisotropic necessity – unit space unit time exchangeable, time given length-scale even anisotropic left default FALSE. nugget Positive numeric jitter added kernel diagonal numerical conditioning. Distinct estimated observation-noise variance, fitted hyperparameter. anisotropic Logical. TRUE least two coordinate axes, fit one length-scale per axis (automatic relevance determination) rather single isotropic length-scale. kernel stays isotropic per-axis-rescaled coordinate space, axis gets correlation range – right model field varies different scales along different directions (east-west tillage gradient versus north-south slope, space versus time axis). Default FALSE (single length-scale, original behaviour). solver Character: "exact" (default) fits exact GP full Cholesky factorisation, cubic number observations. "lowrank" fits Deterministic Training Conditional (DTC) sparse GP n_inducing space-filling inducing points – cost O(n * n_inducing^2) – fields large exact solver. low-rank solver isotropic (single length-scale) falls back exact solver data rows n_inducing. n_inducing Integer number inducing points solver = "lowrank" (default 200, minimum 3); ignored exact solver.
